textbookText: 4. How is hybrid produced? Explain with example.

A hybrid is an offspring produced by crossing two genetically different parents, usually of the same species but with contrasting traits, to combine desirable characteristics from both. For example, in Mendel’s experiment with pea plants, a plant with round seeds (RR) was crossed with a plant with wrinkled seeds (rr), producing F1 offspring Rr, which all showed the dominant round-seed trait. Similarly, in animals, crossing a male zebra with a female horse produces a Zorse, a hybrid combining traits from both parents. Hybrids are important in agriculture and animal breeding for improving quality, yield, and resistance, and in plants, further crossing of F1 can produce F2 generations showing segregation of traits according to Mendel’s laws. 5. Draw a chart show both phenotype and genotype structure of the result obtained in the first and second filial generation of offspring of mouse, having black color and white color according to Mendel's experimental result. With the help of the same chart, write the ratio of phenotype and genotype of second generation.
Ans:- Genotype ratio: 1:2:1 (BB : Bb : bb) Phenotype ratio: 3:1 (Black : White)
6. Draw the chart to show the first generation and second generation results due to the fusion of gamets of long winged

housefly (LL) and short winged butterfly(ll). Which generation shows the law of purity of gamets? Justify it. Ans:- A cross between a long-winged housefly (LL) and a short-winged housefly (ll) produces the first filial generation (F1) in which all offspring are heterozygous (Ll) and show the long-winged trait because long wings (L) are dominant over short wings (l). When the F1 flies are crossed among themselves (Ll × Ll), the second filial generation (F2) shows a segregation of traits: the genotypes appear in a ratio of 1 LL : 2 Ll : 1 ll, and the phenotypes appear as 3 long-winged : 1 short-winged. The law of purity of gametes is demonstrated in the F2 generation because each gamete formed from the F1 heterozygotes carries only one allele (L or l), ensuring that the alleles segregate independently during fertilization and produce the observed genotypic and phenotypic ratios.

7. If the monohybrid cross between black male cat and brown female cat takes place, all offspring of F1 generation were black. Why were there no brown offspring in F1 generation? Show this process with the help of chart upto F2 generation. Write down genotypic ratio of this process. Ans:- When a monohybrid cross is made between a black male cat and a brown female cat, all the offspring in the F₁ generation are black because the black color is controlled by a dominant allele (B), while the brown color is controlled by a recessive allele (b). The black male cat has the genotype BB, and the brown female cat has the genotype bb. During fertilization, each offspring receives one allele from each parent, producing the genotype Bb in all F₁ kittens. Since the dominant allele (B) expresses black color, all F₁ offspring appear black. When these F₁ cats (Bb × Bb) are crossed to produce the F₂ generation, four possible genotypes BB, Bb, Bb, and bb are formed. Out of these, BB and Bb represent black-colored cats, and bb represents brown-colored cats. Therefore, in the F₂ generation, the genotypic ratio is 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb, and the phenotypic ratio is 3 black : 1 brown.

8. Answer the following questions on the basis of Mendel's law. i) In which conditions the ratio of black and white rabbits will be 1:1 from the crossing between black and white rabbits? Justify your answer with the help of chart. Ans:- 1:1 ratio of black and white rabbits occurs when a heterozygous (Bb) is crossed with a homozygous recessive (bb).
